advances: Quantitative control of a fixed positive logarithmic parameter from its supplied full-space marks and actual original volume.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Put $R=U/L$. Rowwise concave Jensen gives
$$
b=\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\int U\,d\rho_i
\le \sum_i\sigma_i U(Y_i)/L_i\le e^\delta .
$$
Logarithmic Jensen gives $b\ge1$. More generally, for any positive integrable $R$ on a probability space $P_0$ with integrable logarithm, set $b=\int R\,dP_0$. Direct change of density gives
$$
D(P_0\,\|\,(R/b)P_0)=\log b-\int\log R\,dP_0,\qquad
\int |R-1|\,dP_0\le b\sqrt{2D(P_0\,\|\,(R/b)P_0)}+|b-1|.
$$
For the second inequality, use the triangle inequality and Pinsker in the convention of $L^1$ distance. To see that constant, group the two laws on a density-difference sign set and its complement. By logarithmic Jensen in each part, their relative entropy dominates the corresponding binary relative entropy. The binary entropy as a function of the first probability $p$ at fixed second probability $q$ has value and derivative zero at $p=q$ and second derivative $1/[p(1-p)]\ge4$. Its lower bound $2(p-q)^2$ gives the squared $L^1$ estimate with constant $2$, with degenerate cases by limits. Here the logarithm mean of $R$ is zero. Multiplying the $L^1$ estimate by $M\max_S L$ yields the claim.

For nonnegative continuous concave $v$ with maximum $m>0$ on a convex body $K$, the homothet of $K$ toward a maximizer by weight $s$ is contained in $\{v\ge sm\}$, hence has volume $(1-s)^d|K|$ for $0\le s\le1$. Integrating the superlevel inequality yields $\int_K v\ge m|K|/(d+1)$, also true when $m=0$. Apply it to $U$ and use $\int_{K_z}U\le M\max_S L\,b$ for the maximum bound.

On the $\varrho/2$ core, each nonnegative concave summand has directional slopes bounded by twice its maximum divided by $\varrho$. For two distinct core points, extend their joining line by $\varrho/2$ beyond each point within $K_z$ and compare the three secant slopes by concavity. Thus $U-L$ is $2B_z/\varrho$-Lipschitz there. If its absolute value at a point of the $\varrho$ core is $A>0$, the ball of radius $A\varrho/(4B_z)\le\varrho/4$ lies in the $\varrho/2$ core and has absolute difference at least $A/2$ throughout. Integrating there and solving for $A$ proves the claim. For bounded $\delta$, $B_z$ stays bounded, and $e^\delta\sqrt{2\delta}+e^\delta-1=O(\sqrt{\delta})$.
statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base with compatible compact convex bodies $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Write $S=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_z$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and $dm=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$, with $M=m(S)$ and $dP_0=dm/M$. Let $L,U>0$ be continuous concave on $C$, with $\int\log L\,dP_0=\int\log U\,dP_0=0$. Suppose finitely many marks $Y_i\in C$, weights $\sigma_i>0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$, and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i}{L_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
$$
If $U(Y_i)/L_i\le e^\delta$ for every $i$, where $\delta\ge0$, then $b=\int(U/L)\,dP_0$ lies in $[1,e^\delta]$,
$$
D\bigl(P_0\,\big\|\,(U/(bL))P_0\bigr)=\log b,\qquad
\int_S |U-L|\,dm
\le M\max_S L\bigl(e^\delta\sqrt{2\delta}+e^\delta-1\bigr).
$$

On any $K_z$, write $B_z=\max_{K_z}U+\max_{K_z}L$, suppressing the base coordinate, and let $\omega_d$ be the unit $d$-ball volume. For every $\varrho>0$ with nonempty core,
$$
\sup_{\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K_z)\ge\varrho}|U(z,x)-L(z,x)|
\le \left(\frac{2\cdot 4^d B_z^d}{\omega_d\varrho^d}\int_{K_z}|U-L|\,dX\right)^{1/(d+1)},\qquad
\max_{K_z}U\le\frac{(d+1)M\max_S L}{|K_z|}e^\delta .
$$
The first estimate on the core applies to any two nonnegative continuous concave functions on a full-dimensional compact convex body, with the zero case $B_z=0$ understood directly. For bounded $\delta$, the certificate thus gives the modulus $O(\delta^{1/[2(d+1)]})$ on any fixed positive-radius core.
title: Quantitative rigidity for a logarithmic contact certificate
